_comment: What the website fetches from the map-data GitHub Release, by release-asset name, through the registry Worker's /content proxy (VITE_OH_PMTILES_URL in .env.web): the three pmtiles as /api/runtime/pmtiles/<key> maps them (<key>.pmtiles), the cities seed, the editor's default world and the stock world. The last two are asked for by name, newest edition first (src/runtime/worldFiles.js), and the names here are those first names, the deep-cleaned editions: regions-seed-clean.geojson (the web-sized seed) and default-regions-names-clean.geojson (the z8 stock world keyed by country names, the file the desktop pins too). The proxy serves only the names in its own table (MAP_ASSETS in the registry Worker); until that table holds these two it answers 404 and the site loads the editions before them, regions-seed.geojson and default-regions.geojson, which the proxy has always known and which stay on the release. This is the list the signed public/content-manifest.json describes, so every entry must be the bytes the release holds under that name: scripts/build-content-manifest.mjs builds the manifest from it, content nodes (Open-Historia/open-historia-node) are filled from it, and server/contentManifest.test.js checks that an asset named here and in scripts/map-assets.json or mobile/map-assets.android.json has the same bytes and sha256 in all of them. The website still fetches the full z10 regions.pmtiles and countries.pmtiles; the desktop (scripts/map-assets.json) and Android lists pin the z8 trims.
